chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf from Saif ibn 'Amirah from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Between every two Adhans there is a sitting period, except for Maghrib, for between them there is only a breath." And it has been narrated that he sits between them in Maghrib, and we have mentioned it later in the Additions.

key_terms.الزِّيَادَاتِ: The Additions (a section in hadith collections containing additional narrations)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time interval between the two Adhans for Maghrib prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to clarify the temporal gap between the first and second Adhan, distinguishing the general practice of sitting from the Maghrib exception where the interval is merely a 'breath' (nafas). This distinction highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the timing of the second call, balancing the Prophet's instruction with the practical reality of congregational readiness, while acknowledging conflicting narrations that permit sitting even for Maghrib.
